questions.q: What does WITH CHECKSUM do during a BACKUP DATABASE operation?
options: Verifies page checksums as pages are read, catching a corrupt page at backup time instead of during a later restore
Compresses the backup file to save disk space
Encrypts the backup file with a checksum-based key
Skips backing up any page that hasn't changed
questions.explain: CHECKSUM has SQL Server verify each page's checksum while reading it for the backup, surfacing corruption early.

questions.q: A differential backup captures changes since which point?
options: The last full backup, not the last differential
The last differential backup only
The last log backup
The moment the database was created
questions.explain: Every differential restates all changes since the last full backup, which is why differentials grow over time.

questions.q: Why does BACKUP LOG fail against a database in the SIMPLE recovery model?
options: SIMPLE recovery automatically truncates the transaction log at each checkpoint, so there's no log to back up
BACKUP LOG requires a special server-level permission not granted by default
SIMPLE recovery databases cannot be backed up at all
BACKUP LOG only works on system databases
questions.explain: SIMPLE recovery doesn't retain log records between checkpoints, so BACKUP LOG has nothing meaningful to capture and errors out.

questions.q: Which query reveals a database's current recovery model?
options: SELECT name, recovery_model_desc FROM sys.databases;
DBCC OPENTRAN;
SELECT * FROM sys.dm_tran_locks;
RESTORE VERIFYONLY FROM DISK = 'backup.bak';
questions.explain: sys.databases exposes recovery_model_desc, showing SIMPLE, FULL, or BULK_LOGGED for each database.

questions.q: What is the practical consequence of a database staying in SIMPLE recovery model?
options: You can only restore to the last full or differential backup — nothing since can be recovered
You can restore to any second in time, just like FULL recovery
Backups become unnecessary because SIMPLE recovery never loses data
Only BACKUP LOG statements are permitted, not BACKUP DATABASE
questions.explain: Without log backups, SIMPLE recovery's worst-case data loss extends back to whatever full or differential backup you last took.
